title: Thirteen DCU tasks report the identical 0.005439 ms for both arms at the default shape, so the paired assay cannot discriminate there
compiler_revision_id: open-cake-ir@0970a36e, open-cake-ir@4278caf2 and open-cake-ir@5151954e -- this record aggregates twenty-seven campaigns that ran at three Compiler revisions, so no single commit is its source; each row of findings/data/2026-09-18-dcu-confirmatory-medians.json names the one its campaign ran at
executor_revision: gfx938@5151954e, gfx938@0970a36e and gfx938@4278caf2 -- the same three, per row; the Executor is built from the same checkout as the Compiler here

evidence.retained: bw1100 campaign evidence for the thirteen tasks whose confirmatory receipts carry the same pooled median for both arms -- absmax_rescale, cosine_similarity, layernorm, layernorm_backward_input, residual_rmsnorm, rmsnorm, rmsnorm_input_gradient, selu, silu, softmax, softmax_backward, softplus_gradient and softsign -- together with the fourteen runs that separated. The two groups cover the twenty-seven qualified runs, which is all of them (F-2026-09-18-003). The medians are retained at findings/data/2026-09-18-dcu-confirmatory-medians.json, one row per task, each row naming the workspace and the content-addressed receipt it was read from so a reader with the host can check a single row rather than the file as a whole. The counts in this record are derived from that file by tests/contracts/test_dcu_medians_counts.py -- not restated here, because restating them is how they went wrong.
sites: those thirteen runs: pooled_medians_ms candidate and baseline both 0.005439, speedup 1.000, classification close_null

The other seven were not computed, so no range is claimed over the whole group; the pair that carries the argument is silu at 1.000 against softmax_backward at 1.500, both reporting 0.005439

the stamp on this record was open-cake-ir@3fa16b8f, a commit no campaign in the table ran at, and one the 4278caf2 campaigns postdate. A single stamp cannot name the source of an aggregate over three revisions, and writing one anyway is what ADR 0065 makes the stamp to prevent: a retained campaign has to be replayable against the tools that produced it, which is a per-campaign fact. It is now recorded per row and the field names all three

observation:
Thirteen operators of different arithmetic report the identical pooled median, to six decimal places, for both arms. The byte counts settle what kind of floor it is: silu moves 1.000 MiB and softmax_backward 1.500, half again as much, and both take 0.005439 ms. Bandwidth-bound work does not do that. Footprints were computed for six of the thirteen, so that pair is the argument rather than a range over the group.

A footprint sweep on the same device says where the floor ends: duration is flat at about 2.4 us below 1 MiB and tracks bytes from about 8 MiB. The task shapes sit in the flat region. So for those thirteen the comparison cannot work -- a candidate that halved the arithmetic and one that doubled it would both report 0.005439, and the paired assay would call both close_null.

Three counts in this record have been wrong, and the corrections belong in it rather than in a later record. The floor count was asserted as seven, then as eleven; the enumeration behind the eleven listed seven tasks and then four more with selu named in both, a union of ten. Separately it said that only three runs rose above the floor and that all three showed the candidate losing. Recounting from the collected medians rather than from the previous sentence gives fourteen separated, and three of those candidates beat their baseline by more than the declared 1.05 materiality (F-2026-09-18-005). Every one of the three was arithmetic about a table, edited from the preceding sentence instead of redone.

The floor count then stood at twelve, over the twenty-six runs whose medians had been collected, with softsign qualified but absent because the host was unreachable. Its receipt has since been read: both arms 0.005439, so it is at the floor. The count is thirteen and the two groups now cover all twenty-seven qualified tasks. Thirteen plus fourteen is that twenty-seven, with nothing left over and no task unaccounted for between this record and F-2026-09-18-003. This is the fourth time this number has moved and the first time it moved because a measurement arrived rather than because a count was redone.

What the separated runs establish is the useful half: the assay resolves this hardware when the kernels cost enough to be resolved. The floor is what these particular kernels cost at this footprint, not the assay declining to resolve anything.

The partition rule is stated in the evidence because it decides the counts and an earlier reading of this record could not recover it: both arms on 0.005439 is 'at the floor', anything else is 'separated'. One arm on the floor therefore separates, which puts prelu and swiglu in the same group by the same rule rather than in different ones, and both are named in the fourteen.

One more correction belongs here because it is the same failure in a different field. This record was stamped open-cake-ir@3fa16b8f, and no campaign it cites ran at that commit; the nine campaigns at 4278caf2 ran after it. The campaigns ran at three revisions -- 5151954e, 0970a36e and 4278caf2 -- and a field holding one commit cannot say that, so it now names all three and each row of the medians file carries the revision its own campaign ran at. A reader replaying a single row needs that row's commit, not the record's.
proposed_change:
Run one task at several shapes on this target and read where the reported time starts tracking the bytes -- that is the smallest experiment that distinguishes a dispatch floor from a small kernel, and it needs no Compiler or Lab change. If the times separate at a larger shape, the DCU task shapes should be chosen above that point, and the choice recorded with the measurement that justified it rather than inherited from the CUDA defaults.

Do not read the thirteen close_null results as evidence that the authored candidates matched their baselines. They are evidence that the assay could not tell, which is a different statement and the one the receipts support. A campaign at a shape below the discriminating range spends provider budget to learn nothing about latency, and that is worth knowing before a sweep rather than after.

This says nothing about correctness: all thirteen passed their five validation cases against the external oracle, and that half of the evaluation is unaffected by the floor. Every count in the paragraphs above is now computed from the retained medians by a test, because three of them were wrong while they were prose.
